title: Trump spent the summer selling a war with Iran. His own agents were on the phone with Tehran the whole time.
body: While the White House was building the case for a war with Iran, ICE was quietly working with the Iranian regime to set up deportation flights. That's the story from internal emails obtained by The Intercept through a FOIA request from the National Iranian American Council. The same government telling the public that Iran was too dangerous to talk to was coordinating with Iranian officials, sometimes through Qatari intermediaries and at times directly, to hand over specific nationals it wanted gone.

Then the machine did what these machines do. On the first flight, ICE put a man on the plane who was never on the list. As one official wrote, "An Iranian national not included on the final manifest we sent to Qatari MOI was boarded on the flight." After a stop in Doha, they sent him to Iran anyway. DHS declined to comment on the mix-up.

Sit with the contradiction. A regime dangerous enough to bomb is somehow a fine partner for a deportation deal. The war talk was never really about the danger. It was about who the danger is useful against. And when the paperwork slips, a real person pays for it in the one country you swore was too hostile to touch.
